cells.place: Vimmalūru.—Copper plates discovered in the village. From the Superintendent, South-Eastern Circle, Visakhapatnam.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village of Kikumūru in Dakṣiṇa-mārga-viṣaya by the king to the temple of Śiva called Chālukya-Bhīmēśvara, obviously after the name of the king, on the banks of the Ganges at Prayāga, for the purpose of granting it in his turn as an agrahāra to Brāhmaṇas. Folays appointed it between the temple and a number of learned Brāhmaṇas.

cells.remarks: Records the grant of land for building a maṭha at Vṛiddhāchalam in the name of the Tuḷuva-Voḷḷia community and the introduction of a system to collect some regular levies from the pilgrims for the purpose of feeding the poor therein. Gives a mythical account of the origin of the Tuḷuva dynasty and refers to the reigns of Vīrūpākṣa-Mallikārjuna, Prauḍhadēvarāya, Achyuta, Veṅkaṭapati, Śrīraṅga and Kṛiṣhṇadēva of Vijayanagara.

cells.remarks: Issued from Piṭhīkā. Gives the genealogy of Harsha from Naravardhana and records the grant of the village called Sīmākaṇḍaka in Kuṇḍadhānī-vishaya in Śrāvastī-bhukti, as an agrahāra to Bhaṭṭa Vātasvāmin of Sāvarṇi-gōtra and Chhandōga-śākhā and to Bhaṭṭa Śivadēvasvāmin of Pārāśara-gōtra. The king states that he later bought the same from Vāmanathva who was enjoying it on the strength of a forged edict. The king is styled here as Paramamāhēśvara. The dūtaka was mahāpramātāra, mahā-sāmanta. Skēndra. The seal was originally engraved by Gōbhata. The contents of mahāśōmapaṭṭalādhikṛita-mahā-sā-malārāja Īśvaragupta. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. I, pp. 67 ff. and ibid., Vol. VIII, pp. 155 ff. and Plate.

cells.remarks: Issued from Bṛhadgrāma. Records the grant of the village of Bhōgīgrāma in the vicinity of the (river) Vēgānadā as an agrahāra to five Brāhmaṇas at the request of the village of merchants (vaṇik-grāma) headed by śrēshṭhin Dam-muka. The ruler is said to have been meditating on the feet of Mahāsāmanta Pāṇḍava-varmmadēva. The writer is Kalhaṇa who was a royal sandhivigrahika Adityadatta. In characters of about the 10th century. Published in Ind. Ant., Vol. XX, pp. 123-24.

cells.place: Three sides of a pillar set up in the compound of the Āñjanēya temple.
cells.date: Śaka 996, Ānanda, Puṣhya śu. 8, S u n d a y=1074 A.D., December 28.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of the village Pariyicha-tīrtha on the southern bank of the Perḍoru to god Laḷakīmāṇḍēśvara situated in the midst of the Eḷachime-tīrtha, for worship and offerings on the occasion of the feeding and clothing of twelve students on the occasion of the Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti by Mahā-maṇḍalēśvara Chidda-Chōḷamahārāja who was governor of Kanne-nāḍu and three other divisions. The donor is a Sēna who had been returning from his expedition against a Sēguna who was defeated and captured. The gift was made over to Sūryarāśi-paṇḍita. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXVI, pp. 69-74.

cells.place: Three sides of a second pillar in the same place.
cells.date: (1) Śaka 956, Śrīmukha, Puṣhya śu. 3, Thursday =December 27, 1034 A.D., Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti occurred three days earlier.
cells.remarks: Records a gift (details not clear) on the first date to the temple of Agastēśvara for feeding the ascetics and for vidyādāna, by mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Jōyimarasa of the Kūṇḍi-viṣaya, while camping at Poṭṭalakere. The gift was made over to Jagadindu-paṇḍita who was the recipient of another gift of land (?) and of income from taxes on the second date by the same donor while he was camping at Dīpāḍi. Did another gift was made by another gift to Viṣṇuvāra-paṇḍita, for the maintenance of a sattra attached to the Mūgatēśvara temple. Published in Telangāṇa Inscriptions, Vol. II, pp. 80.

cells.place: Two sides of a slab in the same place
cells.date: [Śaka 970, Sarvadhāri, Bhādrapada śu. 14, Thursday= 1048 A.D., August 25.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Chavumpalli, situated in Kūḍu-kuḷi-13 of Eḷtapa-90 which was a kampana of Vaḍḍa vaṇa-500, for the sattra attached to the temple of Agastēśvara by Kūḍal-arasa (bearing several epithets) while he was camping at Tīrthapuri in Koḍaregaḍaṇḍu, after his victory over Chakrakūṭa. The donor is described as the worshipper of the feet of... The gift was made over to Vīdhivarmitta, Paḍḍagaruḍa Bijjarasa wrote the record. CE. No. 84 above. Ibid., pp. 76 ff. Badly damaged. Records a gift probably of land to god Agastēśvara, for aṅgabhōga. The record starts with the description of the gift by the queen of the ruling king. Seems to record a subsequent gift to the same temple on the occasion of a solar eclipse.

cells.location: Śrīvaikunṭham
cells.place: Eastern wall of the maṇḍapa to the right of entrance of the Kallappirāṉvim temple.
cells.remarks: Records a gift, by the king, of land made free of taxes in the village of Kōḍai, a hamlet of Śrīvaikunṭham for the celebration of the Vaikāśi festival, abandoned for sometime, commencing on the day of Śaḍaiyam with śīrha on the day of Tiruvādirai, his natal star. Mentions an earlier grant of land for a Vaikāśi festival in the 3rd year of the king, by the chchilai alias Āḷudaiyāṉ Kāḷingarayar of Kārembal alias Muḍikoṇḍaśōla-nallūr in Śevvirukkai-nāḍu figures as the signatory. This is a fuller copy of No. 742, SII, Vol. V.

cells.date: Saka 1101, Vikāri, Puṣya ba. 11, Wednesday = 1179 A.D., December 26.
cells.remarks: Registers gifts of land, oil and oil-mill for a perpetual lamp and for worship and offerings in the temple of Mallikārjunadēva for the merit of Kalideva-gavuḍa and other people who were responsible also for the construction of the temple and of a tank called Iśvarasamudra while they were in charge of Kiriya Haṇame, a śēna of Haḷḷavura, as the feudatories of the Kalachuris of Kalyāṇa. Since Kalideva was administering Eḍevare-70, Jallane-70 and other divisions from his capital at Haḷḷavura-bela-gavaṭṭi. The gift was made after worshipping the feet of Padumarāsi-paṇḍita, disciple of Tripichantadēva of Hiriya Maṭha, who was the guru of the king. Kalideva, son of Kēśirāja-daṇḍanāyaka was governing Banavāsi-12000 from his capital at Baḷḷigāve.

cells.place: Slab called Vīragallu set up in the field of M.B. Gabbi.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 6 matter of land to god Beḷḍēva by Apallabbe, wife of Gōvinda-gāvuṇḍa who was governing Banavāsi-12000 while Ammasa and three others were administering Tiri-gamme as gāvuṇḍas. Also records another gift of 4 matter of land to the same deity on a later date by Lokabbe, wife of Avareavasa who was administering Tirigamme while the four gāvuṇḍas were ruling. Refers to the gift-making karaṇas, and Rājāditya-arasa was governing Banavāsi-12000. The gift land was made over to Nigaṇṭandi, the disciple of Boḷḷavisāda-guṇavar, with the consent of the people of Tirigamme, and Tīrthakara Bhaṭṭāra was engraved on the record on the stone which bears the figure of a Jina at the top. Published in Progress Report of Kannada Research Institute, Dharwar, for 1953-57, pp. 69-70, No. 6.

Mentions dāśēśvara Guṅkarasa, son of Udayāditya-Vīra-Kāḷarasa and grandson of Vīra-Goṅkarasa of the Bāṇa family together made a gift of the village Māruḷige situated in Tenguḷi-nāḍu to god Sōmanātha-Kāḷēśvaradēva of Kāḷige, the capital of Maṇṇeyanāḍu-kāḷige. cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama 31, Vyaya, Chaitra śu. 13, Thursday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records that Kechohamayāṇitya-Bhaṭṭopādhyāya and his wife Dēviyakka constructed a temple at Tengli, installed the image of Mallikārjuna and, with the permission of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Bībbarasa, made gifts for the worship of the god and for the maintenance of the temple. Also records that the donor's eldest son, Peḍḍavēchi-Bhaṭṭōpādhyāya and his wife Sāvitriyakka made a gift of land and a garden for the temple. Further states that his brother Kēśavadēva-bhaṭṭa and his wife Malliyakka made another gift of land and a house from their holding to the same temple.

cells.place: Slab kept near the ruined temple outside the village.
cells.date: Śaka 1100, Vijambi, Āshāḍha su. 10, Monday, Dakshiṇāyana-saṁkrānti =1178 A.D., June 26.
cells.remarks: States that mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Mallidevarasa, son of Hallarasa of Morata made a grant of the village Huṇṇeyahalli situated in the rīvaḍa of Morata to god Pallavēśvara. The grant was made in the Kōḍi-kammaṭa (workshop) (at the temple) of māhēśvara Sambhuvanna. Further records grants of money by the Billa-three-hundred and the prabhus and gāvuṇḍas of Morata-Three-hundred. Also records grant of land and a house-site to Sambhuvanna, the mason Timmōja and the carpenter Mallōja.

cells.remarks: States that when Mallidevarasa was camping at Ayyans, Sōmadeva with his chief queen Mākāladēvi, their three sons, Sōbhana-dēva, Bamma-dēva, Mallidēva and his wife, chief queen Mālāyā, described as the dūtī of god Saptamālikā of Morata installed god Sakalēśvara in the name of Mādirajayya and that Basavaladēvi, Mālāyā's daughter and the wife of Mallarasa made a grant of land for god Mālēśvaradēva. Mallarasa was a son of the Haihaya king Bijja of Modegamūr and to have defeated a certain Hadiga and a general of Bhillama. Cf. Nos. 555 and 556 above.
